questions_and_answers.question_text: When combined with present tense forms, 'seit' and 'seitdem' indicate:

answers.answer: Past time continuing in the present

questions_and_answers.question_text: In 'Seitdem ich einen Wagen habe, fahre ich diese Strecke öfter', what has changed since the speaker got a car?

answers.answer: He drives this route more often
Seit vorigem Monat hat er uns erst zweimal angerufen
Vor zehn Jahren war der Verkehr
Dieses Mal standen mir Tage zur Verfügung
Fahren Sie dieses Jahr an die Nordsee

questions_and_answers.question_text: 'Seit' and 'seitdem' can be used with which verb forms?
The sentence 'Ich war seit 1936 nicht mehr in der Lüneburger Heide' expresses:

answers.answer: I haven't been in the Lüneburger Heide since 1936
I was in the Lüneburger Heide in 1936
I will go to the Lüneburger Heide after 1936
I often go to the Lüneburger Heide

questions_and_answers.question_text: In 'Seitdem wir in München wohnen, gehen wir jeden Monat ins Theater', what does 'seitdem' indicate?

answers.answer: Since we have been living in Munich

questions_and_answers.question_text: True or False: 'Seit letztem Sonnabend ruft er mich jeden Tag an' and 'Seit letztem Sonnabend hat er mich jeden Tag angerufen' can express the same meaning.

answers.answer: They refer to different time periods

questions_and_answers.question_text: In 'Seitdem ich diese Aufträge bekommen habe, habe ich keine Zeit mehr für private Interessen', what is the effect of receiving the orders?

answers.answer: I no longer have time for private interests
I have more time for private interests

questions_and_answers.question_text: When other sentence elements imply a cut-off, which verb form is used with seit/seitdem?

articles.text:
The words seit and seitdem "since"
In Unit 12 we noted that past time continuing in the present can be indicated by a present tense form of the verb together with the word seit and an adverb or dative phrase.
In this unit we have encountered the word seitdem as a clause introducer, or subordinating conjunction:
Seitdem ich einen Wagen habe, fahre ich diese Strecke öfter.
Since I have had a car, I have been traveling this route frequently.
Seitdem, like seit, together with present tense forms of the verb signals past time continuing in the present, both in the clause it introduces and in the main clause.
Here is another example:
Seitdem wir in München wohnen, gehen wir jeden Monat ins Theater.
Since we've been living in Munich we've been going to the theater every month.
Both seit and seitdem may occur in sentences with forms of the past tense or perfect phrase, however:
Seit ihrem letzten Besuch hat sie uns nicht mehr angerufen.
Ich war seit 1936 nicht mehr in der Lüneburger Heide.
Seit vorigem Monat hat er uns erst zweimal angerufen.
Seitdem man angefangen hat, die Gebäude wiederaufzubauen, sind viele Schwierigkeiten eingetreten.
She hasn't called us since her last visit.
I haven't been in the Lüneburger Heide since 1936.
Since last month he has only called us twice.
Since they began to rebuild the buildings many difficulties have arisen.
Notice that in these examples reference is to a specific event, or events, which did or did not occur within a period of time beginning in the past and continuing up to the present.
In this case it is the period of time, whose beginning point is established by the phrase with seit or the clause with seitdem, which has continuing relevance in the present, not necessarily the action or event.
In a few cases seit or seitdem may occur either with a present tense or a perfect phrase:
Seit letztem Sonnabend ruft er mich jeden Tag an.
Seit letztem Sonnabend hat er mich jeden Tag angerufen.
Without further qualification by a following statement, both verb forms may imply exactly the same thing, the continuation of past time in the present with the expectation of continuation beyond the present.
Where other sentence elements imply a cut-off, however, only the perfect phrase is used:
Hier hat es seit Tagen geregnet, und heute regnet es immer noch.
Hier regnet es seit Tagen, und heute regnet es immer noch.
Hier hat es seit Tagen geregnet, aber heute scheint die Sonne wieder.
It's been raining here for days, and it's still raining today.
It's been raining here for days, and it's still raining today.
It's been raining here for days, but today the sun is shining again.
Very frequently both present and past tense or perfect phrase forms of the verb occur in sentences with seitdem:
Wir sind erst einmal im Museum gewesen, seitdem wir hier wohnen.
Seitdem er einen Artikel über zollfreie Spirituosen las, will er nach Helgoland fahren.
Seitdem ich diese Aufträge bekommen habe, habe ich keine Zeit mehr für private Interessen.
We've only been in the museum once since we've been living here.
Ever since he read an article on duty-free alcoholic beverages he has been wanting to go to Helgoland.
Since I received these orders I haven't had any time for my own private interests.
